transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Moreno (Redwood SE), Elliot Byrne (Redwood CSM), Priya Kapoor (CTO, Zenith), Marcus Diaz (SRE Manager, Zenith), Laura Chen (VP Eng, Zenith)

Summary:
Quick follow-up to the 2026-02-14 outage postmortem. Goal: align on RCA, confirm mitigations, agree next steps for reliability and contractual concessions.

Topics:
- Root cause analysis and timeline
- Immediate mitigations and rollbacks applied
- Long-term reliability changes (autoscaler thresholds, pre-warm, canary policy)
- Data/PII concerns and compliance notes
- Commercial/contract implications (Dedicated burst, SLA credits)

Action items (recap in call): see action_items field above

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: ok hey everybody thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight we know you've got execs on the line later so, um, quick agenda review. we want to confirm root cause, what we rolled back, and the timeline for fixes and then commercial next steps. Jules can you start with the tech RCA?
[00:28] Jules Moreno: yeah sure, thanks. so high level, the outage on 2026-02-14 was triggered by a confluence of infra autoscaler churn and a runtime regression in the 2.3.1 deploy. the autoscaler dropped below min healthy because the eviction threshold was overly aggressive after a spike in ephemeral disk pressure, that combined with a small regression in KV cache warmup in 2.3.1 meant we saw a long tail latency spike and token generation timeouts.
[01:05] Marcus Diaz: just to confirm, the autoscaler removed nodes before requests drained? that sounds like it, yeah we saw abrupt 503s and connection resets.
[01:18] Jules Moreno: right, some pods terminated while KV cache was still populating; a bunch of requests hit cold KV and we compounded latency due to a new memory allocation pattern in 2.3.1. the immediate mitigation was rollback to 2.3.0 and increase min replicas to avoid scale-to-zero during high churn windows. we also disabled the disk-pressure-driven eviction until we patch the node agent.
[01:55] Laura Chen: can you explain the "memory allocation pattern"—was that a model change or runtime change?
[02:05] Jules Moreno: it was a runtime micro-optimization intended to reduce peak memory on some models but it changed lazy allocation timing for the KV cache; in most cases it improved throughput, in this workload it delayed first-token readiness which hit tail-latency SLOs.
[02:28] Priya Kapoor: timeline wise, when did 2.3.1 ship to the hosts that serve Zenith?
[02:35] Samir Patel: it was rolled into the multi-tenant pool on 2026-02-12 during our normal rolling deploy. your Dedicated pool wasn't impacted but the routing policy sent a percentage of traffic to compatible hosted nodes as part of our burst policy. we should have prevented that burst routing during a risky deploy, agreed.
[03:05] Marcus Diaz: that routing decision is the core issue for us. if hosted nodes are getting risky changes we need stronger isolation or guaranteed pinned versions.
[03:21] Samir Patel: understood. for short term we gave you a pinned version and increased the Dedicated min warm pool. longer term: enforcements on canary safety gates and burst routing constraints will be in the postmortem deliverable.
[03:42] Elliot Byrne: also to note commercial concessions—Samir, you flagged credits for downtime?
[03:49] Samir Patel: yes we will propose SLA credits; Elliot will follow up with contract team and send a proposal.
[03:56] [00:04:00] Jules Moreno: technical mitigation timeline: rollback completed within 12 minutes after detection, KV-cache cold start mitigation (increasing min replicas) applied at T+25 minutes. we also pushed an emergency node agent patch to stop premature evictions which is currently in canary. the longer-term patch to 2.3.1 to restore safe allocation semantics is targeted for 2026-02-23.
[04:28] Marcus Diaz: can you share the logs and the exact request IDs we saw errors for? we need them for our postmortem and our compliance reporting.
[04:36] Jules Moreno: yes we'll compile the request IDs and attach traces. quick note about transcription: some request IDs in our logs are anonymized but we'll provide correlating trace IDs.
[04:52] Priya Kapoor: from a risk standpoint, is there any data leakage risk? we have PHI in some request payloads and need assurance around encryption at rest and in transit.
[05:10] Samir Patel: no evidence of data exfiltration. data-in-flight was TLS; at rest is encrypted with customer keys where you opted into KMS. safe to state no leak. we'll include audit logs in the postmortem package.
[05:34] [00:06:00] Laura Chen: what about longer-term reliability actions? we need concrete things not just words.
[05:40] Jules Moreno: agreed. proposed items: 1) stricter canary gating for runtime changes, 2) pre-warming policy for KV caches on burst, 3) change autoscaler eviction thresholds and add explicit drain windows, 4) enhanced synthetic tests for tail latency, 5) expanded observability around cache hit/miss and cold-starts.
[06:10] Marcus Diaz: can the pre-warm be deterministic? we want a pre-warm API call so our platform can tell Redwood to pre-warm before big jobs.
[06:22] Jules Moreno: yes there's an API we can extend; we'll scope an endpoint to trigger pre-warm for a set of model routes. action item to spec that.
[06:34] [00:08:00] Elliot Byrne: also we propose a weekly "reliability sync" for the next 6 weeks to ensure rollout and monitoring changes.
[06:42] Priya Kapoor: that would be good. also we need a change freeze window policy—no risky infra changes during our peak windows.
[06:52] Samir Patel: we can agree to a change freeze for your tenant during high-usage business hours, we'll formalize in the runbook and the SLA addendum.
[07:04] Laura Chen: on the commercial side: if we need guaranteed pinned versions, what does dedicated cost look like?
[07:11] Samir Patel: we discussed reserved Dedicated capacity previously; we can send an adjusted quote with burst capacity options and guaranteed version pinning. I'll include optional 24/7 priority support and a lower latency SLO.
[07:28] Marcus Diaz: what's the mitigation for the routing decision that sent traffic to multi-tenant?
[07:34] Jules Moreno: quick fix: we tightened the routing rules so that during a canary deployment we don't route Zenith traffic to newly updated pools. long-term: policy engine will include a tenant isolation flag.
[07:50] [00:10:00] Priya Kapoor: are there any tests we can run jointly to validate the fix before we accept it?
[07:58] Jules Moreno: yes, we'll run a joint benchmark: synthetic tail-latency tests with your traffic pattern, and run the KV warmup pre-warm and measure first-token latencies. propose week of 2026-02-23.
[08:15] Samir Patel: we'll also provide a small credit for the pain and priority engineering time. details in follow-up.
[08:24] Laura Chen: good. for postmortem doc can you include a succinct timeline with exact timestamps? we need that for our audit.
[08:34] Jules Moreno: absolutely. the postmortem doc will include timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, logs, traces, and the remediation timeline.
[08:46] [00:12:00] Marcus Diaz: one ask: will the patch to 2.3.1 be backward-compatible so we can re-enable it, or do we need to skip that version entirely?
[08:55] Jules Moreno: the plan is to restore allocation semantics while keeping memory optimizations; we expect it to be compatible once validated, but until then we won't force upgrade your pinned hosts.
[09:08] Priya Kapoor: can you give a brief explanation of the canary gating improvements? what are the metrics and thresholds?
[09:16] Jules Moreno: we'll add stricter SLO checks for tail latency (95/99th token latency), cache miss rates, and pod churn. if any gate fails, rollback is automated and routing to burst pools is disabled until a manual review.
[09:34] [00:14:00] Elliot Byrne: customer ask: please include SOC 2 and encryption details in the postmortem packet. also include contact for legal if they need it.
[09:43] Samir Patel: noted. we'll attach a security appendix.
[09:50] Laura Chen: moving to acceptance criteria—what do we need to see before we accept the remediation as complete?
[09:58] Jules Moreno: acceptance criteria: synthetic tail-latency tests pass at baseline, no KV cold-starts observed under your load profile for 48 hours, canary pass in our control plane for three sequential deploys, and logging/tracing shipped to you for the incident window.
[10:22] Marcus Diaz: that seems okay.
[10:26] [00:16:00] Samir Patel: commercial next steps: I'll get pricing and SLA credit proposal in 48 hours. Elliot will set up the weekly reliability sync invites. Jules will own the technical artifacts and run the benchmark.
[10:43] Priya Kapoor: one more question—are we going to change retention on request logs? we need at least 90 days for compliance.
[10:53] Samir Patel: retention is configurable; we'll confirm current retention and propose extending to 90 days for the account, we'll need to include cost impact in the proposal.
[11:08] [00:18:00] Laura Chen: any other mitigations like circuit breakers at the request router level?
[11:14] Jules Moreno: yes adding request-level circuit breakers for high-latency routes is on the roadmap; we'll accelerate that for your account.
[11:24] Marcus Diaz: will there be a post-deploy validation suite we can run ourselves?
[11:30] Jules Moreno: yes, we'll provide a validation harness and scripts. action item for Jules to share a GitHub link and instructions.
[11:42] [00:20:00] Elliot Byrne: we're out of time for deep technicals, so quick recap and owners: 
Samir - pricing and credits (due 2026-02-20)
Jules - postmortem doc + logs + runbook updates + benchmark (due 2026-02-20)
Marcus - provide traces and request ids (due 2026-02-19)
Elliot - schedule weekly syncs (due 2026-02-24)

[00:21:05] Priya Kapoor: ok we appreciate the fast response. please make sure the postmortem is actionable and includes dates.
[00:21:18] Samir Patel: will do. thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with the postmortem link and the action items.
[00:21:30] Laura Chen: thanks.

End of transcript.
